# SidStation ASID

> A free, open source audio plugin (VST3, AU and Standalone) that plays the three SID voices of the Elektron SidStation hardware synth from a DAW. It streams raw MOS6581 SID registers over the ASID protocol rather than sending MIDI CC, so each voice gets its own pitch, gate and register writes. One plugin instance drives one voice.

Key facts, since they are easy to get wrong:

- It requires Elektron SidStation hardware. It contains no SID emulation and makes no sound on its own.
- The hardware must be put into ASID mode from its front panel before the plugin can drive it.
- One instance drives one voice, so playing all three voices polyphonically means three instances on three DAW tracks, each set to a different voice.
- ASID is used because the SysEx Direct Program path is dead on OS 1.11 R34 firmware, not by preference. That finding is what shaped the whole design.
- Presets are the plugin's own voice sounds, saved to disk as files that live outside both the DAW project and the unit's own memory.

Current release is 1.1.0 (2026-08-09), licensed GPL v3, by Benjamin Dehli under Dehli Musikk. There are builds for macOS, Windows and Linux. The macOS build needs 10.15 or later, is universal for Apple Silicon and Intel, and is signed and notarized: its AU installs to /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/Components, the VST3 to /Library/Audio/Plug-Ins/VST3, the Standalone to /Applications. Windows ships an Inno Setup installer and Linux an x86_64 tarball, both carrying the VST3 and Standalone (AU is macOS only) and neither signed. Only the macOS build has been tested against real hardware. This is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Elektron.

## Docs

- [Landing page](https://benjamindehli.github.io/sidstation-asid/): what the plugin does, the four tabs (Voice, Wavetable, Modulation, Global), install steps and screenshots.
- [README](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/blob/main/README.md): the same ground in more detail, plus the repository layout and build instructions.
- [Protocol notes](https://benjamindehli.github.io/sidstation-asid/protocol/): what talking to real hardware turned up, including the ASID frame format, the two address spaces, the dead Direct Program path on OS 1.11 R34, and findings from four real patch banks.
- [Protocol source](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/blob/main/core/README.md): the same ground alongside the code that implements it.
- [Releases](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/releases/latest): the signed and notarized macOS DMG, the Windows setup installer and the Linux tarball.

## Source

- [Repository](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid): C++17 and JUCE, built with CMake.
- [core/](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/tree/main/core): framework agnostic library for the SidStation MIDI, SysEx and ASID protocols. No dependencies, has its own tests.
- [asid/](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/tree/main/asid): the plugin, its JUCE UI and its MIDI device layer.
- [probe/](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/tree/main/probe): command line tool for checking the protocol against real hardware.

## Optional

- [Packaging notes](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/blob/main/packaging/README.md): how the installers for all three platforms are built, including the macOS signing and notarization.
- [License](https://github.com/benjamindehli/sidstation-asid/blob/main/LICENSE): GNU GPL v3.
- [Dehli Musikk](https://www.dehlimusikk.no/): the author's music business.
